_comment: One Human Not Present presentation, both hops, pinned as the single string
that travels: the open Checkout Mandate the user signed before leaving, and
the closed one the agent signed as a delegation of it. The mandate vectors
beside this one pin credentials; this pins a delegation, which is a
different artefact and the only one an agent acting alone ever produces.
Two signatures, by two parties: the root with the user's key, the delegating
hop with the agent's. Both are HMAC-SHA256 so the string can be pinned at
all — ECDSA draws a fresh nonce per signature — on the terms
golden_test.go's hmacAuthzKey records.
!! THIS VECTOR DOES NOT EXERCISE THE cnf LINK, AND MUST NOT BE READ AS IF IT
DID. The root's cnf names an EC P-256 key and the delegating hop is HS256
under a different kid. They are not the same key. This chain verifies in our
own suite only because the test's key resolver returns the agent verifier
whatever cnf says. An implementation that resolves cnf to a key, which is
what a conformant verifier does, will reproduce this string exactly and then
reject it as an invalid signature. That is correct behaviour on its part.
Reproduce this string to check your encoding and your sd_hash over the root
as presented. Check the cnf-to-delegating-key link against your own tests,
not against this file. Ours are
TestADelegationSignedWithAKeyTheOpenMandateDidNotEndorseIsRefused and
TestADelegationSignedWithTheEndorsedKeyIsAccepted.
It cannot be made faithful without giving up determinism: a symmetric key is
not admissible in cnf, and the one deterministic asymmetric scheme, Ed25519,
is unavailable to this package under the repository's key-containment rule.
The delegating hop's sd_hash covers the root as presented, so this string
commits to which of the root's disclosures travelled. This one withholds
none of the four: a Merchant can state every fact the constraint registry
holds, so narrowing an open Checkout Mandate for it removes nothing. An
implementation that narrowed it at all, or that narrowed it after signing,
lands on a different sd_hash and a chain no verifier accepts.
checkout_hash is the same digest checkout_binding.json publishes for the
same document, and that equality is not decoration: a closed mandate signed
as a delegation binds its checkout exactly as a standalone one does. The
mandate handed to DelegateCheckout claimed 'not-the-hash' and the value
below is what the adapter recomputed instead.
audience and nonce are part of what the string commits to. A chain minted
for one verifier is not presentable to another, so a reader comparing
serialisations needs to know which verifier this one was addressed to to
tell a drift from a different transaction.
